questions.stem: Rabindranath Tagore was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. For which of the following works was the prize specifically given?

options.option_text: Gora, a novel exploring Indian identity and caste society
Gitanjali (Song Offerings), a collection of devotional poems
The Home and the World, a novel set during the Swadeshi era
Kabuliwala, a celebrated short story set in colonial Bengal

questions.explanation: Gitanjali, Tagore's collection of devotional prose-poems translated into English by Tagore himself, was the work cited by the Nobel Committee. Options A and C are novels Tagore wrote but after the prize; Option D (Kabuliwala) is a short story, not a full literary collection, and was never the basis for a Nobel citation.

questions.stem: Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979. In which city was she born, and what was that territory known as at the time of her birth in 1910?

options.option_text: Kolkata (Calcutta), then capital of British India province
Skopje, then part of the Ottoman Empire's Kosovo Vilayet
Tirana, then part of the declining Ottoman Albanian region
Belgrade, then capital of the Kingdom of Serbia region

questions.explanation: Mother Teresa was born Anjezë Bojaxhiu in Skopje (present-day North Macedonia), which in 1910 was part of the Ottoman Empire's Kosovo Vilayet. Kolkata (Option A) is where she spent most of her life working, which causes frequent confusion. Tirana and Belgrade are the capitals of Albania and Serbia respectively — neither is her birthplace.

questions.stem: Amartya Sen's 1998 Nobel Prize in Economics was awarded for contributions to which specific domain of economics?

options.option_text: International trade theory and the comparative advantage model
Welfare economics and the theory of social choice
Game theory and strategic interaction among rational agents
Monetary economics and modern inflation-targeting frameworks

questions.explanation: The Royal Swedish Academy cited Sen for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory, including work on famine analysis and development as freedom. Option C (game theory) is associated with Nash/Harsanyi/Selten (1994 Nobel). Option A (comparative advantage) is classical trade theory; Option D relates to central-bank frameworks, not Sen's research.

questions.stem: Har Gobind Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Which of the following CORRECTLY describes the contribution for which he was recognised?

options.option_text: Deciphering the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis
Discovering the double-helix structure of the DNA molecule
Identifying restriction enzymes that cleave DNA at specific sites
Developing recombinant DNA techniques used in gene splicing

questions.explanation: Khorana, along with Nirenberg and Holley, was recognised for interpreting the genetic code — how the sequence of nucleotides in mRNA specifies amino acids. Option B describes Watson and Crick's 1962 prize. Option C (restriction enzymes) is the 1978 Nobel work of Arber, Smith, and Nathans. Option D (recombinant DNA) is associated with later work in the 1970s by Berg, Boyer, and Cohen.

questions.stem: The 'Chandrasekhar Limit' (≈1.4 solar masses) — the concept central to Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar's 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics — represents which physical threshold?

options.option_text: Minimum energy needed to initiate hydrogen fusion inside a protostar
Maximum temperature achievable at the core of a main-sequence star
Maximum mass a white dwarf star can possess and remain stable
Critical mass required to trigger a Type II supernova explosion

questions.explanation: The Chandrasekhar Limit defines the upper mass boundary (~1.4 M☉) beyond which electron degeneracy pressure cannot support a white dwarf; the star must collapse into a neutron star or black hole. Option D is a tempting distractor because Type Ia supernovae occur when a white dwarf accretes mass up to this limit — but that is a consequence, not what the limit defines. Type II supernovae involve different physics (iron-core collapse of massive stars).

questions.stem: Fleming, Chain, and Florey shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology for penicillin. Which statement CORRECTLY identifies Howard Florey's specific contribution, as distinct from Fleming's?

options.option_text: Florey first observed that Penicillium mold could kill bacterial colonies
Florey partnered with Chain to purify penicillin for clinical application
Florey determined the beta-lactam ring structure of the penicillin molecule
Florey synthesised the first artificial version of the penicillin compound

questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered in 1928 that Penicillium notatum mold inhibited bacterial growth (Option A describes Fleming, not Florey). Florey and Chain (Oxford team, late 1930s–early 1940s) purified sufficient penicillin to test it clinically and proved it could treat bacterial infections in humans. Option C relates more to Chain's chemical analysis work. Option D (synthetic penicillin) was achieved only in the 1950s–60s, after the prize.

questions.stem: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for determining the atomic structure of the ribosome. Which experimental technique was the PRIMARY method used by his team to achieve this resolution?

options.option_text: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy of ribosome samples
Fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) live-cell imaging
X-ray crystallography of ribosomal subunits at near-atomic resolution
Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) tomographic reconstruction method

questions.explanation: Ramakrishnan's group at MRC Cambridge, along with Steitz (Yale) and Yonath (Weizmann), used X-ray crystallography to determine ribosomal structures at ~3 Å resolution, revealing how mRNA and tRNA bind during translation. Option A (NMR) is unsuitable for molecules as large as the ribosome. Option D (cryo-EM) has become dominant for ribosome work since ~2013 but was not the primary technique used in the prize-winning work. Option B (FRET) is a dynamics tool, not a structure-solving method at atomic resolution.
